name: Elephant
intro: An elephant is the biggest animal on land. It has a long nose called a trunk.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Elephants are the biggest animals on land.
A big elephant is as heavy as a school bus.
It has a long nose called a trunk.
Its big ears help it stay cool.
Its long tusks are really teeth.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Some elephants live in Africa.
Other elephants live in Asia.
They live in grasslands and forests.
Their homes are often very hot.
They spray water and dust on their skin to stay cool.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Elephants are herbivores, so they eat only plants.
They eat grass, leaves, bark, and fruit.
They spend most of the day eating.
They use their trunks to pick up food.
They suck up water in their trunks to drink.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A baby elephant is called a calf.
A new calf is about as heavy as two grown-ups.
A calf can stand soon after it is born.
It drinks its mom's milk for about 2 years.
The family herd helps take care of the calves.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: A calf may suck its trunk like a thumb.
An elephant's trunk has no bones.
Elephants can use their trunks like a snorkel.
Elephants say hello by wrapping their trunks together.
Elephants talk with low rumbles.

vocab.meaning: A long tooth that grows out of the mouth.
A big group of animals that live together.
An animal that eats only plants.
